transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood Solutions), Liam Chen (CTO, Cygnus), Rosa Martinez (Core Infra Lead), Evan Park (ML Eng), Jamie O'Neal (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Cygnus is evaluating Redwood for a streaming assistant used in their analytics dashboard.
- Primary goals: p95 token emission latency <= 350ms, support for 200 concurrent users during peak, and token bursts up to 8k tokens/sec for short windows.
- Constraints: data residency, SOC2 audit, VPC connectivity, on-prem pilot possibility.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. are we good to go?
[00:03] Liam: yep, thanks. can you hear me okay? a little travel noise but fine.
[00:07] Jordan: great. quick intros, i'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. priya is our software/infra SE, Marcus is solutions, they will walk through perf and profiling.
[00:18] Liam: Liam Chen, CTO, with Rosa and Evan and Jamie. we run Cygnus Insights, enterprise analytics assistant embedded in our app.
[00:26] Rosa: hi all. we care about tail latency and also predictable cost. we get big bursts when reports run, some long-form responses.
[00:33] Priya: thanks Rosa. can you describe your production flow briefly? average prompt size, output length, and concurrency patterns?
[00:40] Evan: sure. typical prompt is 120-250 tokens, outputs average 600-1400 tokens, but sometimes 3k tokens for long reports. our interactive product streams token-by-token to the UI. baseline stack is on-prem Kubernetes with a custom gpt-like model serving; evaluating moving to Redwood Dedicated for reliable throughput or Private for data residency.
[01:01] Jamie: timeline is Q3 pilot, Q4 production for a subset of customers.
[01:06] Jordan: perfect. main engineering objectives? p95 SLOs, cost per token, and availability during bursts?
[01:12] Rosa: yes. p95 token emission latency ideally <= 350ms for streamed tokens; end-to-end completion p95 under 2.5s for 800-token responses. concurrency target ~200 active streams in peak across regions with short bursts up to ~8k tokens/sec for 10-30s when customers run batch reports.
[01:30] Marcus: ok that's a good target set. a few clarifying questions: by p95 token emission do you mean the inter-token latency at the client? and are you measuring from client RTT included?
[01:41] Rosa: we measure from our gateway receiving the first token to the client rendering, so includes network hops inside our VPC but not the user's internet. internal RTT to the inference cluster should be included.
[01:50] Priya: good. we typically separate out serving time (runtime) and network time. for streaming tokens, runtime per-token p95 target of ~100-200ms is typical for LLMs in the 7-13B class on modern infra when batched; end-to-end will add routing and queueing.
[02:05] Evan: our model is 13B finetuned, FP16. we care about KV cache reuse across turns, and prefix caching; we also do several reranks post-generation.
[02:15] Jordan: reranks add extra token passes, can you quantify how often reranking runs per request?
[02:18] Evan: 25% of sessions do rerank, usually a 2 to 3 prompt pass with a short scoring model.
[02:24] Marcus: that will multiply token work, so for capacity planning we need to multiply baseline tokens by 1.25 to 1.4 factor.
[02:30] Jamie: we're also sensitivity to cold cache — first request after model swap is painful.
[02:34] Priya: yes. warmup and KV cache priming is important. our Dedicated offering supports pinning models to nodes and background pre-warm, also automatic prefix caching for common prompts. that reduces cold-start p95 dramatically.
[02:47] Liam: talk to me about Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private cost and predictability. we want near-dedicated throughput but don't want to manage operations if we can avoid it.
[02:56] Jordan: short answer: Hosted is lowest friction but shared capacity, fluctuate under noise; Dedicated is reserved GPU pools you own for the duration — predictable latency and throughput; Private mirrors Dedicated but with a customer-controlled control plane and VPC/on-prem options for compliance. cost per token typically lower on Dedicated for high sustained usage.
[03:12] Rosa: do you let us set autoscale thresholds for Dedicated? our concern is sudden peaks.
[03:16] Priya: yes, you can configure autoscaling policies and burst capacity. we support short-lived burst capacity for spikes, we call it burst pools; there's a warm-up time depending on instance types, but you can reserve burst capacity or reserve higher baseline so spikes are absorbed without scale up lag.
[03:30] Evan: numbers — what tokens/sec per GPU do you typically see for our 13B on A100-like hardware with quantization?
[03:36] Marcus: rough numbers, highly workload dependent: 13B FP16 on modern A100/RTX equivalents does ~300-800 tokens/sec per GPU for generation depending on sequence length and attention pattern. with quantized 4-bit and kernel optimizations we can push higher sustained tokens/sec but with some quality tradeoffs. burst throughput can be scaled with more GPUs in Dedicated.
[03:55] Jordan: for streaming p95 targets, we tune batching windows to balance latency vs throughput; for inter-token latency under 350ms p95 we often keep batching latency under 50-80ms and per-token runtime under 150-200ms.
[04:06] Rosa: how much does batching hurt single-request latency? if you batch 50ms you add to p95 right?
[04:10] Priya: yes, batching introduces a tunable added latency equal to batching window or until batch fills. we implement dynamic batching and latency budgets per route so you can set strict SLOs. if you require single-token latency below 200ms we will route those to low-batch lanes.
[04:24] Liam: what about KV cache hit rates — we have many similar queries, can caching reduce cost dramatically?
[04:29] Priya: absolutely. prefix/KV caching for conversational flows and repeated prompt prefixes can reduce token work by up to 60% for high-reuse patterns. we also support per-customer cache TTLs.
[04:39] Evan: we've seen 40-50% reuse in some analytics flows. can Redwood support multi-tenant cache isolation?
[04:44] Marcus: yes, Dedicated gives you isolation; even Hosted has tenant-aware cache partitions. Private on-prem gives you full control.
[04:50] Jamie: security — SOC2, SSO, KMS? we will need audit trails.
[04:54] Jordan: Redwood has SOC2, SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC, KMS integration and audit logs. for Private we can integrate with HSMs. we'll follow up with our compliance pack.
[05:03] Rosa: good. also need network diagrams for VPC peering and egress IP list.
[05:07] Jordan: we'll send that.
[05:09] 
[05:10] -- Deep dive on profiling and benchmarking --
[05:12] Priya: proposed approach: you give us a representative prompt set (golden prompts, distribution of lengths), and a 3x scaled traffic profile that reflects peak+burst. we'll run a Dedicated bench with configurable concurrency profiles: steady-state and burst windows. we'll instrument p50/p95/p99 for token emission and total completion time, and measure tokens/sec sustained and peak.
[05:31] Evan: for burst windows we care about 10-30s spikes to 8k tokens/sec. can you simulate that?
[05:36] Priya: yes, we can run short-duration high-concurrency experiments. two caveats: if you want extremely short <5s microbursts, autoscale won't spin up instantly; reserve burst capacity or provision headroom to absorb them.
[05:49] Liam: what about network egress — do you charge for egress for Dedicated?
[05:54] Jordan: Hosted includes egress in usage, Dedicated typically mirrors cloud provider egress; specific pricing we can map in the spreadsheet. we'll include examples.
[06:05] Rosa: what monitoring do we get? token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, tracing?
[06:09] Marcus: Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route p95, traces, and you can hook custom tracing spans. we also expose an events stream for audit logs.
[06:18] Evan: one more — reranking and additional model passes. can we offload rerank to a small CPU or low-GPU model to keep cost down?
[06:24] Priya: yes. typical pattern: use smaller embedder or ranking model on CPU if latency allows, or route to a lower-cost model variant for rerank. Redwood supports model variant routing and automatic fallback.
[06:36] 
[06:37] -- Numbers and capacity examples (rough) --
[06:38] Marcus: concrete sample: assume average output 1k tokens, average generation tokens/sec per GPU 500 for your prompt shapes. without caching and with 200 concurrent streams you need roughly: 200 active * 1000 tokens / (500 tokens/sec per GPU) = 400 GPU-seconds per second, which is not direct but to reach sustained you need ~8 GPUs to keep up (this is rough). add rerank factor 1.25 -> ~10 GPUs. For bursts of 8k tokens/sec sustained across cluster, that's ~16 GPUs at 500 tokens/sec each.
[07:06] Rosa: that math helps, but we need cost per hour to compare.
[07:10] Jordan: we'll include cost calc in spreadsheet using your traffic profile. Dedicated reserved pricing reduces unit cost compared to Hosted.
[07:16] Evan: what about quantized models — can we compress to 4-bit and improve throughput? what quality loss should we expect?
[07:22] Priya: 4-bit (Q4) quantization gives big memory and throughput gains; for many flows it is near-transparent, but depends on your finetuning. we'll recommend an A/B with metrics on hallucination/regression and rouge-like scores. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization candidates.
[07:36] Jamie: can we do gradual rollouts and canaries?
[07:39] Marcus: yes, Canary deployments, A/B routing, and automatic fallback to a safe model variant if quality drops. rollout policies are in Console.
[07:47] 
[08:00] -- Live Q&A and gotchas --
[08:02] Liam: what's common pitfall you've seen for teams moving from self-host to Redwood Dedicated?
[08:06] Priya: under-provisioning for concurrent prefixes and rerank; not accounting for KV cache warm-up; assuming autoscale covers instant microbursts. Also sometimes teams forget network egress configs and NAT mapping for peered VPCs.
[08:20] Rosa: do you support on-prem appliances? some regulated customers require air-gapped options.
[08:24] Jordan: yes, Redwood Private includes an on-prem package and private control plane options. we'll need to discuss support model and enterprise contract.
[08:31] Evan: any constraints with model size? if we want to run 70B for some customers is that supported?
[08:36] Marcus: yes, larger models are supported but tokens/sec per GPU will be lower. for 70B you'll need significantly more GPUs and different tuning; Dedicated can be provisioned accordingly.
[08:45] 
[08:47] -- Agreement on next steps --
[08:48] Jordan: to recap next steps: we'll run a Dedicated profiling window with your prompt set, send the throughput spreadsheet, and share SOC2 and Private deployment diagrams.
[08:57] Liam: good. can we get the profiling session scheduled next Tue?
[09:00] Priya: I have an opening Tue 11:00 UTC, we can do a 2-hour slot to run profiling and watch metrics live.
[09:06] Rosa: i'll need to coordinate a maintenance window for VPC peering but that should be fine.
[09:11] Jordan: excellent. action items noted. any final questions?
[09:15] Evan: one: will you expose token-by-token latencies in the console?
[09:18] Marcus: yes, Console exposes token emission times, per-route p95, and traces for individual requests.
[09:24] Jamie: thanks all. excited to see numbers.
[09:27] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and test plan.
[09:31] -- call ends --

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., K-V cash -> KV cache, may show speaker label drift). This export keeps time markers about every 15-60s and retains conversational disfluencies.
